Loss-of-function variants in TSC1 or TSC2 disrupt the tuberous sclerosis complex, leading to hyperactivation of the mTOR signaling pathway. This dysregulated pathway contributes to abnormal neuronal proliferation and migration in the cortex, causing focal cortical dysplasia (Disease A), and abnormal smooth muscle cell proliferation in the lungs, leading to lymphangioleiomyomatosis (Disease B).

partners.mechanism_chain: TSC1 (HGNC:11540) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); TSC2 (HGNC:11541) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); MTOR (HGNC:7109) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Focal cortical dysplasia (HP:0002379); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0033731); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Hamartoma (HP:0003272). Mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 lead to the loss of their inhibitory function on the mTORC1 complex, causing its hyperactivation. Similarly, mutations in MTOR itself can impair its proper regulation or function. This aberrant mTOR signaling disrupts normal cellular processes including proliferation, differentiation, and migration, leading to the characteristic histopathological features of focal cortical dysplasia (FCDII) and the formation of hamartomas and other neurological manifestations seen in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC1).

falsification.text: The discovery of pathogenic variants in TSC1, TSC2, or MTOR in patients with isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than a loss-of-function or hypomorphic effect impacting mTOR pathway regulation, would falsify this hypothesis. partners.diseaseBName: lethal congenital glycogen storage disease of heart
partners.mechanism_chain: TSC1 (HGNC:11771) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP409); TSC2 (HGNC:11772) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP409); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP409) —LEADS_TO→ Focal cortical dysplasia (HP:0002377); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP409) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart disease (HP:0001627); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP409) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Loss-of-function mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 lead to the hyperactivation of the mTOR pathway. This dysregulated mTOR signaling contributes to abnormal neuronal development and proliferation, resulting in focal cortical dysplasia. Concurrently, hyperactive mTOR signaling promotes excessive protein synthesis and potentially abnormal glycogen metabolism or storage within cardiomyocytes, leading to cardiomyopathy and congenital glycogen storage disease of the heart.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. lymphangioleiomyomatosis  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.736)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1632852, Reactome:R-HSA-165181, Reactome:R-HSA-380972, Reactome:R-HSA-5628897, Reactome:R-HSA-8854214)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in TSC1/TSC2 (null) —DISRUPTS→ TSC1 (HGNC:11749); Pathogenic variant in TSC1/TSC2 (null) —DISRUPTS→ TSC2 (HGNC:11750); TSC1 (HGNC:11749) —DECREASES→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP43); TSC2 (HGNC:11750) —DECREASES→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP43); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP43) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0002374); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP43) —LEADS_TO→ Lung cysts (HP:0002088). Loss-of-function variants in TSC1 or TSC2 disrupt the tuberous sclerosis complex, leading to hyperactivation of the mTOR signaling pathway. This dysregulated pathway contributes to abnormal neuronal proliferation and migration in the cortex, causing focal cortical dysplasia (Disease A), and abnormal smooth muscle cell proliferation in the lungs, leading to lymphangioleiomyomatosis (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TSC1 or TSC2 that are associated with gain-of-function effects in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the mTOR pathway with rapamycin analogs has shown efficacy in treating some manifestations of tuberous sclerosis complex, suggesting potential therapeutic strategies for both focal cortical dysplasia and lymphangioleiomyomatosis.

#### 2. tuberous sclerosis 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1632852, Reactome:R-HSA-165181, Reactome:R-HSA-380972, Reactome:R-HSA-5628897, Reactome:R-HSA-8854214)

**Proposed mechanism:** TSC1 (HGNC:11540) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); TSC2 (HGNC:11541) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); MTOR (HGNC:7109) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Focal cortical dysplasia (HP:0002379); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0033731); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); mTOR signaling pathway (WP:WP720) —LEADS_TO→ Hamartoma (HP:0003272). Mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 lead to the loss of their inhibitory function on the mTORC1 complex, causing its hyperactivation. Similarly, mutations in MTOR itself can impair its proper regulation or function. This aberrant mTOR signaling disrupts normal cellular processes including proliferation, differentiation, and migration, leading to the characteristic histopathological features of focal cortical dysplasia (FCDII) and the formation of hamartomas and other neurological manifestations seen in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC1).

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in TSC1, TSC2, or MTOR in patients with isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, rather than a loss-of-function or hypomorphic effect impacting mTOR pathway regulation, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, evidence showing complete functional independence of the disease mechanisms from the mTOR pathway would refute this link. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of TSC1, TSC2, or MTOR in gnomAD that are strongly associated with either disease would challenge the rare variant hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** The shared dysregulation of the mTOR pathway provides a strong rationale for investigating mTOR inhibitors as a potential therapeutic strategy for both isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II and tuberous sclerosis 1.

#### 3. lethal congenital glycogen storage disease of heart  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.422)

Concurrently, hyperactive mTOR signaling promotes excessive protein synthesis and potentially abnormal glycogen metabolism or storage within cardiomyocytes, leading to cardiomyopathy and congenital glycogen storage disease of the heart.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of independent, non-overlapping molecular pathways for each disease, or evidence that TSC1/TSC2 mutations do not impact mTOR signaling in a manner consistent with both phenotypes. _(variant: No common variants (AF > 1e-4) in TSC1 or TSC2 associated with a loss-of-function effect.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the mTOR pathway could offer a therapeutic strategy for both focal cortical dysplasia and certain forms of congenital heart disease characterized by metabolic dysfunction.
